- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to avoid premature bottoming.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until price stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment trend direction but reduce magnitude by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model, consider lagged sentiment: if sentiment was negative 5–7 days ago, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 10 days.
